title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: HubSpot
providers.scope_notes: Private-app and newer developer-platform static authentication coexist. SSO requires eligible Professional/Enterprise subscriptions.

controls.name: Legacy private app scopes
controls.what: Super Admin selects which scopes the private app token can use; editable after creation.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Scopes / Edit app
controls.quote: select the **checkbox** for each scope you want your private app to be able to access.

controls.name: Legacy private app token Rotate
controls.what: Issues a new token and expires the old one immediately or after 7 days; Super Admins get a reminder after 180 days without rotation.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Auth > Rotate
controls.quote: If your token is compromised and you want to immediately revoke access, click **Rotate and expire now**.

controls.name: Delete legacy private app
controls.what: Deleting the app permanently revokes its access token.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Auth > Delete
controls.quote: When you delete one of your private apps, its access token will be permanently revoked and you'll no longer be able to use it to make API calls.

controls.name: Super Admin required for private apps
controls.what: Only Super Admins can access and create private apps, so withholding Super Admin removes the ability; there is no account-wide off switch.

controls_unknown: No IP allowlist for API calls found; "Allowed login IPs" (Settings > Security > Login) is documented only for logins.
Whether app governance (approval) covers privately distributed OAuth apps and static-auth apps, or only HubSpot Marketplace listings.
No admin-set token lifetime or mandatory rotation policy found for private app tokens, static tokens, service keys or the developer API key (only manual rotation and reminders).
No account-wide switch found to block service key creation other than withholding Developer tools access / Super Admin.

authentication.summary: Static access token for a legacy (non-project) private app, sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. HubSpot implements it on top of OAuth, so client libraries accept it as an access token.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Trusted-IP documentation restricts account logins; API-call enforcement for private-app/OAuth tokens was not established.

renewal.summary: Rotate the private-app token explicitly, immediately or with a 7-day transition.

administration.summary: Super admins manage legacy private apps: scope selection, viewing and rotating the token, 30-day API call logs, and deletion (which revokes the token). Super admins get rotation emails and a reminder after 180 days without rotation. Removing the user who created the app can make some calls fail until the token is rotated.
administration.conditions: UI creation of new legacy private apps is disabled on 2026-09-28 for accounts created on or after that date and on 2026-10-26 for older accounts; existing legacy private apps keep working. HubSpot points new in-account integrations to service keys (hubspot-5). Migrating a non-project legacy private app to platform 2026.09 is not currently supported. Up to 20 private apps per account.

offboard.details: Removing the user who created the private app makes some (not all) API calls with its token fail.

inventory.details: Super admins see private apps under Development > Legacy apps; GET /account-info/v3/api-usage/daily/private-apps reports usage for all private apps.

reads.ui: Development > Legacy apps > {private app} > Logs tab; Method = GET, search request URL '/crm/v3/objects/contacts'; Export logs (CSV) for 30 days

offboard.ui: Settings > Users & Teams > {user} > Actions > Deactivate user, then Actions > Remove from account

token_format.notes: Static bearer token, does not expire unless rotated. Prefix not shown in fetched private-app docs (service keys use pat-na1-). GitHub secret scanning covers 'Hubspot Private Apps User Token'.

log_sources.name: HubSpot security activity (Account activity API /account-info/v3/activity/security)
log_sources.notes: Records user actions such as PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW and INSTALL_INTEGRATION with IP/location. UI shows 30 days; export covers last year. Scope account-info.security.read.

log_sources.name: HubSpot centralized audit log (/account-info/v3/activity/audit-logs)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise only. User actions incl. CRITICAL_ACTION subcategories. Records HubSpot-user actions, not API calls.

log_sources.name: Private app Logs tab (API call logs)
log_sources.notes: Per-app API calls for 30 days; filter by method/response/URL; CSV export. No request body, URL params or response payload for successful calls.

credential_id_fields.notes: Private app ID on PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW (also in infoUrl /private-apps/{hubId}/{appId}/auth)
Private app ID on CRITICAL_ACTION / PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW
Maps a found token to its private app, plus userId (creator), hubId, scopes

lifecycle_events.notes: A user revealed the token in the UI (security activity type / audit subCategory). Possible exfil point.

anomaly_cues: PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW by a user who does not own the integration, or from a new country/IP
Token view followed within hours by API calls in the Logs tab from new patterns (new endpoints, export-heavy reads)
Private app whose creator was removed (calls failing with USER_DOES_NOT_HAVE_PERMISSIONS) yet still active
Token not rotated in 180+ days (HubSpot reminder emails)
Scopes broadened on a private app with no change ticket

containment.steps: Private app > Auth > Rotate > 'Rotate and expire now'; or delete the private app (token permanently revoked). Then update the integration with the new token.
containment.notes: 'Rotate and expire later' leaves the old token valid for 7 days; use expire now for incidents.

sample_query.purpose: Find who revealed private app tokens, from where, before a suspected leak.

calls.log_notes: Shown in the private app's Logs tab for 30 days; request body, URL parameters and response payload are not stored; rate-limit-exempt calls are not logged.
